headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 3 studies yielded an effect size of 0.7 (95% CI: 0.38–1.27), indicating no statistically significant association between lutein and bladder cancer. sample_size.excerpt: We investigated the association between plasma carotenoids and vitamin C and risk of urothelial cell carcinoma (UCC) in a case-control study nested within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition. A total of 856 patients with newly diagnosed UCC were matched with 856 cohort members by sex, age at baseline, study center, date and time of blood collection, and fasting status.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 856 + 856 = 1712

cases.excerpt: We investigated the association between plasma carotenoids and vitamin C and risk of urothelial cell carcinoma (UCC) in a case-control study nested within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition. A total of 856 patients with newly diagnosed UCC were matched with 856 cohort members by sex, age at baseline, study center, date and time of blood collection, and fasting status.

effect_size.excerpt: Plasma lutein was inversely associated with risk of nonaggressive UCC (IRR: 0.56; 95% CI: 0.32, 0.98; P-trend = 0.05).
